q: How much of the FY2026 topline comes from renewals?

r.narrative: About 62% of JIMDO's FY2026 topline is renewal business: EUR 38.2M of main-plan renewal net sales after credit memos plus EUR 6.6M of addon renewals, out of EUR 72.0M in the ML Baseline. New business adds EUR 27.2M — and every new subscription becomes a renewal cohort 12 or 24 months later, so FY2027 renewals grow to EUR 47.0M.
r.sql:
SELECT YEAR(c.PERIOD) AS FISCAL_YEAR, SUM(c.RENEWALS) AS RENEWED_PRODUCTS, SUM(c.NEW_SUBS) AS NEW_SUBSCRIPTIONS
FROM SDP_JIMDO.PUBLIC.JIMDO_COHORT_SERIES c
WHERE c.IS_ACTUAL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

r.narrative: The leak is the first renewal. In FY2026, customers renewing for the first time retain at about 71% against 79% for older cohorts — an 8-point gap. It is widest on Dolphin START (68.5% first renewal), in France (69.2%) and Japan & ROW (69.5%); 24-month plans retain lowest at their first renewal (66.3%).
r.sql:
SELECT s.REGION, s.ITEM,
       SUM(c.POTENTIAL_YOUNG * c.RET_YOUNG) / NULLIF(SUM(c.POTENTIAL_YOUNG), 0) AS FIRST_RENEWAL_RETENTION,
       SUM(c.POTENTIAL_OLDER * c.RET_OLDER) / NULLIF(SUM(c.POTENTIAL_OLDER), 0) AS OLDER_RETENTION
FROM SDP_JIMDO.PUBLIC.JIMDO_COHORT_SERIES c JOIN SDP_JIMDO.PUBLIC.JIMDO_SERIES s USING (SERIES_ID)
WHERE c.IS_ACTUAL AND c.PERIOD >= '2025-08-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3;

q: What is a 1pp retention improvement worth?

r.narrative: Each extra point of retention across all forecast cohorts adds about EUR 0.74M of FY2027 main-plan renewal net sales after CM, and the effect compounds because retained customers become next year's older cohort. The workbook's +2pp multiplier from 2027 is therefore a EUR 1.5M decision — the ML forecast supports about +1pp without a dedicated retention programme.

q: How accurate is the ML forecast versus the workbook?

r.narrative: On a 12-month backtest (trained to July 2025, forecasting August 2025 to July 2026), the ML forecast predicts renewals within 0.78% against 2.80% for the workbook's flat trailing-12-month retention — 72% less error. The workbook over-forecasts by 2.7% because it holds retention flat through the 2025–26 consumer-confidence dip; the ML bias is 0.5%. History is generated and calibrated to the FC Summary, so this illustrates the method; on JIMDO's actual orders the same pipeline gives the real comparison.
r.sql:
SELECT WORKBOOK_WAPE, ML_WAPE, WORKBOOK_BIAS, ML_BIAS, WORKBOOK_MAE_PP, ML_MAE_PP
FROM SDP_JIMDO.PUBLIC.V_JIMDO_BACKTEST_SUMMARY;

q: How does the ML Baseline differ from the Workbook Baseline?

r.narrative: The ML Baseline keeps the workbook's logic but takes retention and new subscriptions from SNOWFLAKE.ML.FORECAST (consumer confidence, price steps, SME formations, ad cost) for 12 months. It lands FY2027 topline at EUR 85.5M against EUR 84.4M in the Workbook Baseline (+EUR 1.1M), almost all in renewals (EUR 47.0M vs EUR 45.9M) as confidence recovers after the 2025–26 dip.

FROM SDP_JIMDO.PUBLIC.JIMDO_PLAN_VERSION ORDER BY VERSION_ID;
